title: Long Bennington III Memorial
crew_summary: 7 killed including pilot Plt Off. Cedric Arthur Chapman

external_narratives.summary: Detailed account of the loss of Lancaster LM311 on 12/13 July 1943. The aircraft was severely damaged by flak over Turin and on return to base suffered structural failure when flaps were lowered, breaking in two. Chapman reported having no elevator control and was flying on trimmer only.
key_details: Returning from bombing raid on Turin
Flak damage forward of tail section
Structural failure when flaps lowered for landing
Pilot reported no elevator control, flying on trimmer
Three of 18 squadron aircraft lost that night
external_narratives.link_description: Explore detailed account of Lancaster LM311's loss in 1943 due to severe damage from flak and structural failure upon landing.

external_narratives.summary: Comprehensive local history account of Lancaster LM311's last flight from RAF Bottesford with 467 (RAAF) Squadron. Documents the seven crew members and the circumstances of the crash near Long Bennington village.

Details the crew composition: P/O Chapman (RAAF pilot), Sgt Michaels (navigator), Sgt Smith (bomb aimer), Sgt Donlevy (W/Op AG), Sgt Greenwood (flight engineer), F/Sgt Bruce (mid-upper gunner), Sgt Buchanan (rear gunner).

memorial_details:
Name: Avro Lancaster LM311
Type: Board / Plaque / Tablet
Description: A metal plaque attached to a backboard, mounted on a rough hewn stone on a concrete base. Lettering is incised and picked out in black. The plaque refers to a memorial tree, probably a Eucalyptus planted in 1995. By 2015 an immature sapling was recorded, presumably having replaced the original tree. By December 2020 the sapling was no longer in evidence (presumed dead).
Inscription: 467 RAAF SQUADRON ASSOCIATION/ This tree was planted in memory of/ the Crew of Lancaster PO-L LM311/ which crashed on return from Turin/ 13th July 1943/ [crew names inscribed on memorial]/ We shall Cherish their Memory
Location: West along a farm track off Costa Row Costa Row Long Bennington South Kesteven Lincolnshire NG23 5G England

Memorial Unveiling: The unveiling of the Avro Lancaster LM311 memorial.

Eucalyptus Tree Planting (1995): A tree was planted with a plaque near the graves of aircrew from Bottesford Airfield who were killed in action.
narrative: On a bombing operation with 467 (Australian) Squadron, Lancaster LM311 departed RAF Bottesford on 13 July 1943. The aircraft sustained severe flak damage during the mission and suffered structural failure upon returning to base, coming down near Long Bennington, Lincolnshire. Pilot Officer Chapman, who piloted the Lancaster, was among the seven crew members killed in the crash. Also lost were Flight Sergeant William Bruce, Sergeant Jack Greenwood, Sergeant Albert Edward Michaels, and Sergeant Norman Campbell Smith. Sergeant Greenwood was 25 years old at the time of his death.

This account is presented in an anonymous account and photograph permanently on view in Bottesford Parish Council Rooms, donated by former members of 467 Squadron to mark the 50th Anniversary of the end of WW2 in 1995.
